semantic_correction.stem: A client is unable to get out of bed while the linens are changed. Which bed-making technique is appropriate?

options.A: Use an occupied-bed technique, keeping the client covered while safely rolling from side to side and replacing the soiled and clean linens one half of the bed at a time.
options.B: Postpone the linen change until the client can transfer out of bed, even when the linens are soiled, so the mattress can be made without repositioning the client.
options.C: Remove the bed linens before preparing the replacements and leave the client uncovered briefly, then reposition the client after the clean linens are placed on the mattress.
options.D: Assist the client to stand at the bedside for the linen change when possible, because an occupied-bed technique is less safe than a brief supported standing transfer.

semantic_correction.rationale: A is correct. Current NCBI/Open RN Nursing Assistant guidance provides a specific occupied-bed technique for a person who remains in bed during linen changes. The checklist instructs caregivers to provide privacy, roll the resident safely toward a raised side rail, roll the soiled linens toward the center, place clean fitted and lift linens on the exposed half of the bed, then roll the resident to the opposite side so the soiled linens can be removed and the clean linens pulled through. The resident is kept covered during the procedure, and postprocedure safety includes checking comfort, keeping the bed low and locked, and placing the call light within reach. Therefore the appropriate method is the occupied-bed technique with safe side-to-side repositioning and staged linen replacement. B is incorrect because soiled linens should be changed rather than deferred until the client can get out of bed. C is incorrect because the resident's privacy and coverage should be maintained and the linens are changed in stages rather than removing everything first. D is incorrect because a client unable to get out of bed should not be required to stand for linen changes when an occupied-bed technique is specifically designed for this situation.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Use the occupied-bed technique to change linens safely for a client who must remain in bed while maintaining privacy, coverage, safe side-to-side repositioning, and postprocedure safety.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests safe occupied-bed linen changing with one clearly best technique, balanced alternatives, current source verification, and no absolute-word or length cue.

option_audit.A: Correct. It directly matches the occupied-bed checklist's staged linen replacement, side-to-side rolling, and maintenance of coverage and privacy.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Soiled linens should be changed when needed rather than delayed until the client can leave the bed.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. The occupied-bed technique maintains privacy and coverage and changes linens in stages rather than removing all linens before replacements are ready.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. The occupied-bed method exists specifically for clients who remain in bed and avoids requiring an unsafe or unnecessary standing transfer.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A uniquely matches the occupied-bed method; B delays necessary hygiene, C compromises privacy and sequence, and D requires mobility the stem states the client does not have.
cueing_check: All four options are parallel bed-making approaches of comparable length and specificity; the prior 'all' distractor and uniquely-long correct response were removed.
